title: Head heavy rackets: weight at the head, suited to attacking play
text: A head heavy racket shifts its weight towards the head of the racket. It suits an attacking style because it produces powerful, steeply downward smashes.

title: Head light rackets: weight at the handle, suited to defense and counter-attack
text: A head light racket shifts its weight towards the handle (grip). That is why a head light racket feels light and is easy to maneuver, which suits a defensive, counter-attacking style.

title: Even balance rackets: suited to beginners
text: An even balance racket distributes its weight evenly. It suits beginners, or players who are still looking for their preferred style of play.

title: How shaft stiffness affects power and control
text: The shaft connects the racket frame to the handle. When you clear, smash and so on, your force bends the shaft, and it snaps straight again right as it meets the shuttlecock. In other words, the power of the shuttle = your hitting force + the elastic force released as the shaft bends. So the stiffer the shaft, the more control the player has over where the shuttle goes, because the shuttle's power depends more on your own hitting force, and the reverse is true for a flexible shaft.

title: Shaft stiffness types: stiff, flexible and medium
text: Shafts are rated by stiffness and come in 3 types: stiff, flexible and medium. A stiff shaft is less elastic and gives less assistance, but you control the force and the accuracy of the shuttle better. A flexible shaft is the opposite of a stiff one: it gives more assistance but makes the shuttle harder to control. A medium shaft balances stiff and flexible.

title: Stiff rackets are not suitable for beginners
text: A stiff racket is not 'friendly' to new players, because it requires the player to swing quickly and powerfully. It is suited to players who are already solid in the basics of swinging and striking.

title: Racket weight classes 3U, 4U and 5U
text: 3U, 4U or 5U indicates the weight of the racket. The smaller the U, the heavier the racket, and vice versa. A low U racket withstands force well and suits people who like powerful smashes and hard-hitting shots, but it tires the arm more easily. The higher the U, the more agile and easy to handle the racket is. Most players choose a 4U racket.

title: Grip size G2 to G5
text: G2, G3, G4, G5 - the grip circumference of a badminton racket indicates how thick the handle is, which directly affects how it feels in your hand. The smaller the G, the thicker the handle, which suits people with large hands. The larger the G, the opposite, which suits small hands. Currently the most common sizes are G4 and G5.

title: How a beginner should choose a racket, depending on arm strength
text: A new player who already has strong arm strength should start with a slightly head heavy to head heavy racket with a medium shaft. A player whose arm strength is not yet good will usually be better suited by a head light to even balance racket with a flexible to medium shaft.

title: When and how an intermediate player should change rackets
text: An intermediate player should change rackets once they have good fundamentals in badminton (how to swing, footwork to reach the shuttle at the optimal position, the correct grip for forehand and backhand strokes, etc.) and have decided which style of play they want to move towards. If you choose attack, switch to a slightly head heavy to head heavy racket with a stiff shaft for fast, explosive power and accurate shuttle placement. If you choose defense and counter-attack, a head light racket that is agile to maneuver together with a stiff shaft helps the shuttle go accurately and exactly where you intend.

title: String tension: effect on power and accuracy
text: The string is the part strung into the racket frame that makes direct contact with the shuttlecock. String tension is measured in pounds or kg. The higher the string tension, the less assistance it gives and the more arm strength you need, but the shuttle goes more accurately. The lower the string tension, the more assistance it gives, but the accuracy of the shot drops significantly.
